facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's terms of reference state that DHIS2, which manages aggregated health information mainly for epidemiological surveillance and has been implemented for routine epidemiological management since November 2018, is in operation in all structures of the national health service, which it lists as two central hospitals, four regional hospitals, 32 health centres, 34 health posts and 114 basic health units among others; no date is given for the position, so the document's published date is used.

The Ministry of Health's terms of reference name DHIS-2 as one of the three main information systems in use by the ministry, with its Health Technology, Communication and Information Office (GTCIS) leading the digital health work; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.

The Ministry of Health's terms of reference state that Medicine One, the proprietary clinical information software brought in with the Electronic Prescription Project to centralise clinical history in a single electronic repository, is in use only in Praia's health facilities, namely its health centres and the central hospital, because of its complexity, per-workstation licence costs and bandwidth needs; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.

The Ministry of Health's terms of reference name Medicine One as one of the three main information systems in use by the ministry, a proprietary-code product for which licences are paid per workstation and per period; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.

The Ministry of Health's terms of reference state that the government's digital governance strategy (EGDCV) and its action plan take health as a priority and include the single-platform health project, under which the ministry plans a platform for a single electronic clinical process on IGRP Web for all health structures, public and private; the National Digital Health Strategy itself was still to be written, by a consultant working within 120 days under a commission created on 30 May 2023; the document's published date is used.
